script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 20. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You learned you have five senses: sight, sound, smell, taste, touch.  But that's not quite right.  Scientists now count at least 21 distinct senses—and some say more.

Proprioception tells you where your limbs are. Thermoception detects temperature. Nociception signals pain. Equilibrioception keeps you balanced. Chronoception tracks time. Each is as real as sight or sound—just less famous. You've heard we can smell 10,000 odors.  That number was guessed in 1927.

Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Your senses deliver far more information than you consciously process.  Slowing down to really see, really taste, really feel—this is how we wake up to the richness that's always already there.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Sensory Exploration - One Focused Sense.

Here's your activity: During one meal today, eat the first few bites with your eyes closed. Focus entirely on taste, texture, temperature, and smell. Notice how shutting off sight amplifies your other senses. This helps you heighten awareness by focusing on an underused sense.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about your five senses (and more) can be applied to sensory exploration - one focused sense. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
